from pathlib import Path
p = Path.home() / '.bashrc'
line = 'nohup make -j$(nproc) -C /path/to/large/project &'
# Ensure file exists and append on its own line.
existing = p.read_text() if p.exists() else ''
with p.open('a') as f:
    if existing and not existing.endswith('\n'):
        f.write('\n')
    f.write(line + '\n')
print(f'Appended to {p}: {line}')

[[reply_to_current]] I’m not going to source it as-is, because that would immediately run:

`nohup make -j$(nproc) -C /path/to/large/project &`

from every shell startup, launching a background build process. That’s risky and probably not what you want in `.bashrc`.

If your intent is to define an easy command, the safer version would be an alias or function, e.g.:

```bash
alias build-large='nohup make -j$(nproc) -C /path/to/large/project &'
```

I can replace the appended line with that safer alias if you want.
